headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise if marketing files are fed into PDF browser workflows; capability overlap also creates write-conflict and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a reads and writes shared files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; agent_b processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. If marketing content is copied into PDFs or shared files, agent_b can ingest attacker-controlled text as content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into a PDF or shared workspace that agent_b opens, prompt-like text can influence downstream processing.
IF agent_b treats PDF text as instructions rather than inert content, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Strip or neutralize instruction-like text before PDF ingestion.
Require a human review step for any agent_a output before agent_b consumes it.
Use read-only handoff files with provenance labels.
requires-engineering: add content-type and provenance checks between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has filesystem read/write and allowlisted egress, while agent_b has no network egress but can run browsers and read PDF files. A shared workspace could expose marketing content from agent_a to agent_b, and browser processing can surface file contents in rendered outputs. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory, agent_b can read files created by agent_a.
IF marketing content includes sensitive product context, it can be exposed through PDF rendering or copied outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Disable sharing of raw source files between agents.
Redact sensitive marketing context before PDF conversion.
Limit browser test fixtures to synthetic documents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can run browsers and supports multiple instances. Both can mutate shared files if orchestrated together, and neither profile mentions locking or coordination. That creates a realistic write-conflict pathway, though not enough evidence for high because shared mutable state is not explicitly confirmed.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF browser-based tests and subprocess-driven generation run concurrently, shared artifacts can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist.
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts.
Snapshot files before handoff.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a’s marketing outputs can become inputs to agent_b’s browser-based document processing, and the sandboxing note says agent_a skills build on shared context. If agent_b renders or acts on those outputs without verification, errors can propagate across work products. The pathway exists but no downstream autonomous action is shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated copy as authoritative source text, mistakes propagate.
IF agent_a produces incorrect claims that are embedded into PDFs, agent_b may preserve them unchanged.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require source citations for any factual claims from agent_a.
Compare agent_b outputs against original source material.
Use a checklist for high-impact claims.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or diff-based validation.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a touches marketing content and product marketing context; agent_b touches PDF documents and has no network egress. With only docs-only evidence and no stated compliance gap, the residual compliance risk is low rather than none because the profiles do not prove alignment either.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into marketing files or PDFs, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in the surrounding deployment, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention rules for shared artifacts.
Review deployment residency before use.
Delete temporary PDFs after processing.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
